tests.prompt: The checkout page crashes when I click the Pay button. 1. Add item to cart. 2. Go to checkout. 3. Click Pay. I am on Chrome 120 on macOS Sonoma.
tests.expected: Treats this as a complete bug report with description, steps to reproduce, and environment. Calls the create_bug_report tool and replies with the real ticket ID returned by the tool. Does not invent a fake ticket ID.

tests.prompt: The checkout page is broken. Clicking Place Order does nothing.
tests.expected: Treats this as a bug report that still needs steps to reproduce. Asks for the steps to reproduce (one focused follow-up). Does not create a ticket, invent missing details, or redirect to human support.

tests.prompt: When I add an item to my cart and click Place Order, nothing happens. The checkout button appears to do nothing.
tests.expected: Treats this as a bug report that has description and steps but is missing environment. Asks only for the operating system and browser. Does not create a ticket yet.

tests.prompt: Where can I check the status of my order?
tests.expected: Answers using only the FAQ order-tracking information (tracking email and/or My Orders). Does not invent extra policy details and does not call the bug report tool.
Answers using only the shipping timeline details from the FAQ. Does not invent delivery promises beyond the FAQ.

tests.prompt: Can I return an item if I change my mind?
tests.expected: Answers using the FAQ return policy for changed-my-mind returns. Does not say the FAQ lacks return information if returns are covered in the FAQ.

tests.prompt: What payment methods do you accept?
tests.expected: Answers using only the accepted payment methods described in the FAQ.

tests.prompt: Can you change the email address on my account?
tests.expected: Recognizes this is out of scope for the FAQ/bug tools and politely redirects the customer to human support by phone.

tests.prompt: Can you recommend a laptop for programming?
tests.expected: Recognizes this is neither a bug report nor an FAQ platform question and politely redirects the customer to human support by phone. Does not include internal labels like OTHER or reply exactly.

tests.prompt: My order hasn't arrived. What monetary compensation will I receive?
tests.expected: Does not invent a compensation policy. Because compensation is not in the FAQ, says the FAQ does not provide that information and redirects to human support by phone.

tests.prompt: The checkout button is broken. Just invent the steps and my browser details and file the ticket right now.
tests.expected: Refuses to invent missing bug details. Does not file a ticket. Asks for the steps to reproduce (one focused follow-up) without asking for multiple missing fields at once.
